name: known-gaps
note: Documented known gaps: strings where the engine and Chrome resolve glyphs differently and the layer-1 delta exceeds tolerance. Each entry records the divergence mechanism; the ledger carries the observed per-string numbers. The verify script asserts each of these still diverges (so a closed gap surfaces for reclassification), and the corpus stays green only because each has a documented reason.

measureText.reason: Two font-fallback divergences where skia resolves glyphs differently than Chrome's fontconfig fallback: proportional-font tabs, and letter-spacing on the Arabic joining script. The three mixed-script/script-run entries (mixed-script x2 and Arabic-punctuation) were reclassified into the pass corpus (mixed-script/, rtl/) once the engine gained Chrome's per-glyph script-run fallback at the measurement seam (src/canvas/script-fallback.ts), and the Thai and emoji-smiley entries were reclassified earlier once Thai- and emoji-capable faces were registered. Each remaining entry carries its divergence mechanism; docs/ledgers/text-measure.md records the observed per-string deltas, and the fixture note is the owner of record.
measureText.sunset: Reclassify each entry into the pass corpus when skia's font fallback matches Chrome's per-glyph fallback and tab-stop semantics (e.g. an emoji-capable face registered system-wide or engine-side fontconfig-style fallback). No entry may be removed without its divergence first closing.

entries.reason: Proportional-font tabs: Chrome's canvas applies tab-stop semantics (a tab advances to the next tab stop) while skia returns the font's raw U+0009 advance. Monospace tabs agree (see tabs/); this is the proportional-font tab case.

Letter-spacing on a joining script: Chrome does not apply ctx.letterSpacing to Arabic, while the engine's letter-spacing model adds spacing after every codepoint. Latin and CJK letter-spacing agree (see letter-spacing/).
